children: Forum Gandhi Mumbai: IndiGo and Air India Group will shift 133 weekly international departures from Mumbai's Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport (CSMIA) to Navi Mumbai International Airport (NMIA), with most of the flights serving destinations in West Asia including Jeddah, Riyadh, Dammam, Doha among others, people familiar with the matter said.

The shift will move capacity equivalent to close to three million passengers a year to the new airport, accounting for about 60% of the five-million-passenger annual capacity reduction planned at CSMIA for the redevelopment of Terminal 1, sources said. Capacity equivalent to about two million passengers a year remains to be addressed. On Sunday in statements, IndiGo and Air India Group outlined plans to progressively move international services to NMIA over the coming months.

The transfers will allow airlines to maintain services while the redevelopment at CSMIA requires a reduction in operating capacity. IndiGo will transfer 12 daily international departures from CSMIA to NMIA, covering existing services to Bahrain, Riyadh, Dammam, Jeddah, Madinah, Kuwait, Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah, Muscat, Dhaka and Jakarta.

It plans to introduce a daily service to Kathmandu, taking its international network at NMIA to 12 destinations between February and July 2027. In a joint announcement, IndiGo and Adani Airports said they were in the "final stages of operationalizing" the plan.

IndiGo will also transfer the domestic connectivity required to support its international operations from NMIA. Final dates remain subject to project coordination and operating approvals. Air India Group will shift seven daily departures, people familiar with the matter said. Air India Express will begin operating four daily domestic flights from NMIA in December 2026.

It plans to introduce services to Kuwait, subject to approvals, and operate existing services to Oman from January 2027. The airline will progressively transfer services to Jeddah, Riyadh, Dammam, Doha, Muscat and Sharjah, with the transition expected to be completed by the IATA Northern Summer 2027 season.

The shift comes as CSMIA prepares to redevelop Terminal 1, which currently has capacity for about 15 million passengers annually. The rebuilt terminal is planned to handle 20 million passengers a year, with reopening targeted for March 2030. The airport operator has said airlines' historic slots will be restored after the terminal reopens.

However, international airlines including Emirates and Air France KLM have expressed reservations to move capacity to the airport. Discussions with other airlines are continuing, with a meeting scheduled for October 28 and further talks expected in November ahead of the November 4 deadline for filing summer-schedule slots. Sources said Akasa Air could also reach a decision on moving some operations to NMIA soon. The Airline Operators Committee Mumbai has previously said airlines have not agreed to a unilateral transfer of international operations or reductions in existing CSMIA slots and has sought details of airport capacity during the redevelopment.

title: IndiGo, AI to Shift Flights to Navi Mumbai Airport
